# Commission a Tern Relay

This guide is for a technician installing an environmental-telemetry relay at a newly wired site. Commissioning happens through the appliance's local Ethernet service port. A cloud connection is not needed, so the local checks can be completed before the site's upstream network is available. Keep a handover record while working so the next operator can identify the appliance and distinguish a configured radio from a verified collection path.

## Start the appliance

Apply power and allow up to 90 seconds for the power-on self-test. Watch the indicator during this interval. A steady amber indicator means local setup is ready. Open http://192.0.2.1 in the service laptop's browser and enter the one-use enrollment code from the sealed installation envelope. This code enrolls the local appliance; it is not the password for a cloud account.

If the indicator flashes red, stop commissioning and record the displayed fault code for hardware support. Do not use the amber-ready instructions to interpret a flashing red condition. The fault code provides the information hardware support needs to identify the failed self-test.

## Set the site identity

Enter the assigned site ID. Site IDs contain exactly eight uppercase ASCII letters or digits. Select Apply to save the identity. Applying the change restarts the radio and can take up to 30 seconds. The local Ethernet connection remains available during this restart, so continue using the same browser connection to observe the appliance.

The serial number is printed on the underside label. Copy it into the handover record while the label is accessible. Record the site ID there as well; these identify the installation independently of the current packet-counter reading.

## Observe the radio

Open Diagnostics and inspect the radio state. A completed installation must show Joined. Diagnostics also exposes the packet counter used to confirm that the relay is collecting telemetry. The state and the counter answer different questions: Joined confirms radio participation, while a counter increase confirms observed collection during the verification interval.

## Installation materials and local access

Before applying power, attach the supplied antenna and connect the chassis earth lead. Verify that the supply is 24 V DC. Attaching the antenna after power-on is not an approved commissioning sequence. These preparation steps apply even when the technician intends to use only the Ethernet service interface at first.

Bring the sealed installation envelope and a laptop with browser access. Set the laptop's service-port address to 192.0.2.10/24. The relay's service interface has no DHCP server. If the page is unreachable, check the static address and the Ethernet link rather than waiting for an address lease.

## Close out the visit

For the collection check, record the Diagnostics packet counter, wait five minutes, and verify that the counter increased. There is no required final counter value. Enter the observed increase in the handover record alongside the site ID and appliance serial number. Commissioning is complete only when the radio has shown Joined and the packet counter has increased during the check. A saved site identity alone is not evidence that the collection path has been verified.
